hero.title: Albion Online Beginner's Codex
hero.description: Master resource gathering for Albion East (Asia server). Specific spots for T2–T6 in Royal Continent and T7–T8 in the Outlands, with up-to-date gear meta.

essentials.title: Beginner Essentials
essentials.description: The things every new player needs to know — mount, food, refining, and a checklist for your first hour.

firstHour.title: First Hour Checklist
firstHour.subtitle: Step-by-step for your very first hour in Albion
firstHour.intro: Brand new account? Follow these steps in order. After this checklist you'll have a working character, gathering tools, and a clear path forward.

steps.title: Finish the tutorial
steps.detail: Run through the starter quest in your first town — it teaches movement, combat, gathering basics.

steps.title: Pick a starter city
steps.detail: Lymhurst (Wood/Forest), Fort Sterling (Ore/Mountain), Bridgewatch (Hide/Steppe), Martlock (Stone/Highland), Thetford (Fiber/Swamp). Pick what you want to gather.

steps.title: Open the Destiny Board
steps.detail: Press 'J'. This is your skill tree — every action levels nodes. Focus on ONE gathering line.

steps.title: Buy basic gathering tools
steps.detail: Visit the Marketplace, buy the T3 Journeyman tool for your chosen resource (around 200–500 silver).

steps.title: Gather in Blue Zones first
steps.detail: Blue zones = no PvP loss. Find nodes on the map (axe icon = wood, pickaxe = ore, sickle = fiber, knife = hide, hammer = stone).

steps.title: Spend Learning Points (LP) wisely
steps.detail: Press 'J' → click any node → spend LP to skip half the grind. Save LP for your main gathering line.

steps.title: Buy Pork Omelette food
steps.detail: Pork Omelette doubles your carry capacity for heavy resources. Cheap and essential.

steps.title: Get a Riding Horse (T3 mount)
steps.detail: Walking is slow. Even a T3 horse is fast and cheap.

steps.title: Gather, deposit, repeat
steps.detail: Fill bag → return to town → deposit in bank or sell at marketplace. Aim for T4 gathering within a few hours.

steps.title: Join the Adventurer's Challenge
steps.detail: Press 'Y'. Daily quest list with FREE silver, gear, and a Backpack of Insight — easy XP. Do these every day.

tips: Don't buy Premium until you've played 5–10 hours and confirmed you enjoy the game.
Asia server prime time is 13:00–15:00 UTC (9 PM WIB). Off-peak hours have less competition.
Stay in Blue/Yellow zones until you've gathered T4 resources comfortably.
Don't carry valuables when exploring new zones — scout first.

mount.title: Mount Guide
mount.subtitle: Pick the right mount for your activity
mount.intro: Mounts are essential — speed is survival. Each mount has different stats: speed (escape), HP (durability), and carry capacity (haul more loot). Match the mount to your task.

rows.name: Riding Horse
rows.note: Cheapest mount. Slow speed but better than walking.

rows.name: Transport Ox
rows.note: Highest carry capacity — but very slow and easy to gank. Only use in Blue/Yellow.

rows.name: Swiftclaw
rows.note: Fast mount + 1 burst speed skill. Affordable T5 escape mount.

rows.name: Direwolf
rows.note: Fast + has a slow skill that can stop chasers. Popular gatherer choice.

rows.name: Spectral Bonehorse
rows.note: High HP, can summon a wall to block enemies. Great for escape from group ganks.

rows.name: Saddled Eagle
rows.note: Air mount — passes terrain easily. Excellent for guild logistics.

rows.name: Stalker Horse
rows.note: Has stealth invisibility cast — gather and disappear from view.

rows.name: Mistwolf / Moose / Dire Boar
rows.note: T8 mounts for specialized PvP/PvE roles. Expensive and crafted from rare materials.

tips: Always bring a backup mount when gathering — your main mount can get killed.
Match mount tier to your gear tier — don't ride a T6 mount with T4 gear, gankers will target you.
Direwolf or Spectral Bonehorse is the sweet spot for solo Black Zone gathering.
Spent-condition mounts can be repaired at any city's Repair Station for cheap.

food.title: Food & Potion
food.subtitle: Buffs every gatherer must use
food.intro: Food and potions give massive buffs — but most beginners ignore them. Always eat before gathering and keep potions in your consumable slots.

foods.name: Beef Sandwich
foods.useCase: Solo gatherer in Red/Black Zones for survival

potions.name: Resurrection Mage Potion
potions.useCase: Gatherer ESSENTIAL — saves your gear from gankers

potions.name: Invisibility Potion
potions.useCase: Scout dangerous zones or escape ambush

tips: ALWAYS carry Pork Omelette in your consumable slot. Eat before entering a node area.
Resurrection Mage Potion is non-negotiable when gathering in Red/Black Zone — it can save your full loadout.
Sticky Potion is the cheapest way to escape a chaser — toss it behind you while sprinting.
Buy food/potions from city Marketplaces. Don't craft yourself unless you specialize in cooking.

refining.title: Refining 101
refining.subtitle: How to earn 21–43% bonus from city specialty
refining.intro: Selling raw resources is okay. Selling REFINED resources is 5–20× more profit. Every Royal city has a specialty that gives a HUGE bonus when refining the matching resource there. This is THE easy money trick most beginners miss.

steps.title: Gather raw resources
steps.detail: Wood Log, Iron Ore, Stone, Hide, Fiber — pick one and stack T4–T6.

steps.title: Travel to the matching specialty city
steps.detail: For wood → Lymhurst. For ore → Fort Sterling. Check the bonus table above.

steps.title: Find the Refining Station
steps.detail: Each city has a building for its specialty: Sawmill (wood), Smelter (ore), Stonemason (stone), Tanner (hide), Weaver (fiber).

steps.title: Bring lower-tier refined material if needed
steps.detail: T5+ refining REQUIRES the previous tier's material. Example: T5 Steel Bar = T5 Iron Ore + T4 Steel Bar. Buy what you don't have at Marketplace.

steps.title: Refine — claim your bonus
steps.detail: City specialty bonus is automatic in the right city. You'll see +25% return shown in the refining UI.

steps.title: Sell refined material
steps.detail: Sell at the same city's Marketplace OR transport to Caerleon Black Market for higher prices (but risky travel).

tips: Refining gives more Fame per resource than gathering — double benefit.
Caerleon Black Market BUYS items from NPC at high prices — easy silver for refined goods.
Use Travel Planner mod / map to find the safest route to your specialty city.
DON'T refine in your home city if it isn't the specialty city — you waste the bonus.
Stack large quantities before refining (200+ raw materials) to minimize trips.

zones.title: Zone Types Manual
zones.description: Understand the world before you step out. Each zone type has different PvP rules, loot consequences, and farming opportunities.

items.name: Blue Zone (Safe)
items.death: No item loss. Just respawn at the nearest city. PvP is not allowed — attackers get heavy reputation penalty.
items.bestFor: Brand new players, tutorial, T2–T4 gathering, crafting practice, learning controls.
items.access: Around all 5 Royal cities (Lymhurst, Fort Sterling, Bridgewatch, Martlock, Thetford) and Caerleon.
features: Mob & resource nodes T2–T4
No PvP, no full-loot
Safe spot for AFK / casual play
Bank, marketplace, repair stations all here

items.name: Yellow Zone (Knockdown)
items.death: Knockdown only. Gear takes durability damage but you keep everything. PvP is allowed.
items.bestFor: Practicing PvP without losing gear, T3–T5 gathering, learning escape mechanics.
items.access: One ring out from Royal cities (between Blue and Red zones).
features: Mob & resource nodes T3–T5
Full PvP allowed — but no item loss
Killer takes heavy reputation hit
Perfect zone to test escape kits

items.name: Red Zone (Full Loot)
items.death: FULL LOOT. Every item in your inventory can be picked up by the killer. Equipped gear is destroyed.
items.bestFor: T4–T6 gathering, solo Hellgates, intermediate PvP, faction warfare.
items.access: Outer ring of Royal Continent, between Yellow and Black zones.
features: Mob & resource nodes T4–T6
Full-loot PvP enabled — bring only what you can afford to lose
Killer takes reputation penalty (unlike Black Zone)
Faction warfare for silver and tokens

items.name: Black Zone (Outlands)
items.death: FULL LOOT. No reputation penalty for the killer. The most dangerous zone in the game.
items.bestFor: T6–T8 gathering, large-scale PvP (ZvZ), Castle / Territory fights, Hellgates, Avalon raids.
items.access: Through portals from Royal Continent or Cluster portals inside the Outlands.
features: Mob & resource nodes T6–T8 (best loot in the game)
Full-loot PvP with zero penalty
Most players travel in groups (guilds, gangs)
Territory / Castle controlled by guilds for resource access

items.name: The Mists
items.death: Depends on Mist tier — Lethal Mists are full-loot, lower Mists are knockdown.
items.bestFor: Solo gathering T5–T7, Mist Boss farming, solo PvP without large-group risk.
items.access: Random Mist portals spawn in any zone — enter for solo-only instances.
features: Solo-only instanced zones (1 player per Mist)
Lethal Mists = full-loot equivalent
Roaming Mist Boss with rare drops (Vanity items, T8 chests)
Exit through Mist portal back to original zone

items.name: Roads of Avalon
items.death: Full loot. Same rules as Black Zone.
items.bestFor: Group gathering T7–T8, group PvP, dynamic exploration, ZvZ ambushes.
items.access: Avalonian portals open randomly in Royal and Outlands clusters.
features: Dynamic random connection map — refreshes daily
Faction-free PvP — anyone can attack anyone
T6–T8 nodes + unique Avalonian mobs and chests
Roads connect distant zones — great for shortcut travel

items.name: Hellgate
items.death: Full loot inside the gate. PvP is instanced (1v1, 2v2, or 5v5).
items.bestFor: Solo / small-group PvP content, demonic shards, fame & silver source for non-gatherers.
items.access: Hellgate portals spawn in Red and Black zones — enter for instanced PvP arena.
features: 1v1 Corrupted Dungeons, 2v2 / 5v5 Hellgates
Fight a demon boss while watching for invading enemy team
Demonic Cores + tokens for rare gear
Closed Hellgate = no invader (PvE only); Open = PvP enabled

mistakes.title: Common Mistakes (DON'T)
mistakes.description: The biggest mistakes new players make — every one of them costs hours of frustration or silver. Avoid these and you skip past 80% of beginner pain.

items.title: Spread Learning Points across every line
items.detail: Wastes LP. Focus ONE gathering line (e.g. Lumberjack) to T6 first, then branch out. Specialization > spread thin.

items.title: Carry valuable gear into Black Zone
items.detail: If you die, you lose EVERYTHING. Bring only the loadout you can afford to replace 5–10 times.

items.title: Buy Premium on day one
items.detail: Play 5–10 hours free first. Premium pays off only if you actually commit to the game. Easy regret if you quit early.

items.title: Solo gather during prime time (13:00–15:00 UTC)
items.detail: Asia server is packed with gankers. Off-peak (21:00–09:00 UTC) is way safer for solo.

items.title: Skip the Resurrection Mage Potion
items.detail: Resurrection = saves your entire loadout from a single gank. Mandatory in Red and Black zones.

items.title: Refine in the wrong city
items.detail: You skip the +25% specialty bonus. Always refine wood in Lymhurst, ore in Fort Sterling, etc.

items.title: Use high-tier gear to gather low-tier resources
items.detail: Wasteful. Match gear tier to resource tier — T6 gear for T6 nodes, T4 gear for T4 nodes.

items.title: Stay solo forever (no guild)
items.detail: Guilds = group content, Castle/Territory access, faster learning, protection. Solo only ceiling is much lower.

items.title: Travel without a backup mount
items.detail: Your main mount can die mid-gank. Always carry at least 2 mounts in your bag.

items.title: Carry stacks of silver while traveling
items.detail: Silver also drops on death in Red/Black. Store in bank before risky travel.

items.title: Enter a new zone without scouting
items.detail: Always scout the next zone with Invisibility Potion / fast mount before committing. Saves countless deaths.

items.title: Tunnel-vision on the node — ignore mini-map
items.detail: Gankers approach silently. Check mini-map every 5 seconds. Red dots = enemies; even one new dot = exit immediately.

items.title: Forget the daily Adventurer's Challenge
items.detail: Free silver + Backpack of Insight + reputation. Takes 10 minutes. Skip it = lose hundreds of thousands of silver per week.

items.title: Use combat gear in Blue Zone
items.detail: Blue Zone has no PvP. Wear gathering set (Hellion, Hunter) for yield bonus — combat gear is wasted slots.

survival.title: Gank Avoidance & Escape Manual
survival.description: Solo gathering = solo survival. Pros don't avoid danger — they prepare for it. This is the difference between losing one loadout per week vs ten per day.
preGather: Mount HP at 100% — repair before leaving city
Food slot: Pork Omelette active (eat BEFORE gathering)
Consumable slot: Resurrection Mage Potion (non-negotiable in Red/Black)
Escape kit equipped in slot 2 (Stalker Hood + Assassin Shoes)
Backup mount in inventory (Riding Horse minimum)
Silver and rare items deposited at bank — bring only what you need
Plan exit route BEFORE entering — note the nearest portal cluster
Scout the cluster first with Invisibility Potion or fast mount
spotting: Unfamiliar player gear set + skull mount = combat-ready, not a gatherer
Player lingering at chokepoints (portals, cluster edges) without gathering
Multiple players in a cluster without forming a visible group (silent gang)
Player tries to 'befriend' or follow you persistently — classic bait
Sudden teleport-in via Invisibility Shrine or stealth cape
Mini-map red dots moving in a coordinated formation toward your node

escapeKit.why: Throw behind you — slows chasers significantly
7 seconds of invisibility — last resort exit

qSwap: Setup: Gathering gear in main slot, Escape Kit in slot 2
While gathering: Press Q to instantly swap to Escape Kit
Mount up + cast Invisibility (Stalker Hood) the moment ganker appears
Run to portal — once on mount, you're 80% safer
survival.chasedTitle: If You Are Already Being Chased
chased: Mount UP immediately — even a Riding Horse is faster than running
Trigger Stalker Hood Invisibility to break their target lock
Drop Sticky Potion behind you to slow chasers
Sprint toward the nearest portal cluster (not deeper into BZ)
If dismounted: use cape active (Spectral Bonehorse Cape wall, etc.)
Z-out (dismount) and run on foot if mount is about to die — sometimes faster
tips: Always set up Q-Swap before entering any zone above Yellow.
Mount tier should be ≥ gear tier — never ride T3 mount in T6 gear (gankers will target).
Don't be greedy with the last node — exit when inventory is 70% full, not 100%.
Cluster exit timer is ~5 minutes after entry — plan for early exit during gank attempts.
Use cluster Z to escape silver burden — the wall mechanic blocks pursuers.

mists.title: Mists & Roads of Avalon
mists.description: The most under-rated content in Albion. Solo gathering and PvP T4-T8 with way less risk than open Black Zone. Perfect for newbies bridging from Yellow Zone to T8 farming.
mists.intro: Mists are personal instanced cluster — when you enter, you only meet other solo players (1v1 or duo). Roads of Avalon are dimensional shortcuts connecting Royal Continent ↔ Outlands with permanent and shifting portals.

mistsRows.best: Newbie solo gather practice + first PvP exposure

mistsRows.loot: T5-T6 nodes, Tome of Insight drops
mistsRows.best: Build LP + T5-6 fame solo without ganker risk
Real silver income from T6-7 ore/hide/fiber

mistsRows.loot: T7-T8 enchanted nodes, rare Avalonian gear
mistsRows.best: End-game solo farming, best ROI for solo players

knightfall: Spawns randomly in T7+ Mists clusters (~30-45 min interval).
Solo boss fight — drops unique Avalonian artifact + tome chest.
Recommended gear: T6+ self-heal build (Hallowfall, Carving Sword, or Bloodletter Off-Hand).
Don't engage with gear below T6 — wipe risk is high.
Post-kill loot: Avalonian Shards (craft Avalonian gear), Tome of Insight, rare artifact.
roads: Shifting portal clusters connecting Royal ↔ Outlands ↔ random Mists.
Permanent portals in Royal cities (Caerleon T6 portal) stay stable.
Random portals in Outlands create shortcuts between zones — pros use them to avoid known gank routes.
Avalonian energy nodes spawn randomly in Roads — gather them for Avalonian gear refining.
Cluster types: Tunnel (long path), Hub (multi-portal node), Camp (loot + mobs).
portalTypes: 🌟 Wisp Portal (white): exits back to nearest Royal city. Safe.
💀 Skull Portal (red glow): exits to random Outlands — high risk, high reward gear.
🟣 Avalonian Portal (purple): enters Roads of Avalon — connection to special content.
🟢 Static Portal (green ring): consistent exit to specific zone (usually marked on mini-map).
If unsure which portal is safe, check mini-map first — exit destination is usually marked.
energy: Special resource from Roads of Avalon + T6+ Mists.
Used to refine Avalonian gear (T4-T8 enchanted version) — the second-highest tier of gear in the game.
Drops from Avalonian mobs (Avalonian Mage, Avalonian Knight) + energy nodes.
Stack and sell at Caerleon Black Market for max profit.
tips: Mists = YOU ONLY FACE 1-2 OPPONENTS. Way different from Black Zone where 5v1 gank squads roam.
Bring Sticky Potion + Stalker Hood + Royal Shoes — cheap but effective escape kit.
Every time you enter Mists, scout the mini-map before gathering. Other players show as red dots.
Mists reward solo activity — pro-gathering here is more profitable per hour than BZ gathering in groups.
Roads of Avalon = shortcuts. Plan your route in advance — saves 5-10 min of travel per session.
Knightfall Abbey loot worth 100k+ silver per kill — if you find one, engage with a T6+ self-heal build.

faq.title: Beginner FAQ
faq.description: Most common questions newbies ask. Click each question to expand the answer.

items.q: Do I need Premium to play Albion?
items.a: No, you don't. Albion is genuinely F2P viable — many pro players run pure F2P. But if you play > 20 hours/week or actively trade > 1M silver/week, Premium pays itself back via fame/silver/tax bonuses. Suggestion: play 50 hours as F2P first, then decide. See 💎 Premium Math in the Optimize tier for details.

items.q: I died in Black Zone with T6 gear, what now?
items.a: Unfortunately gear is lost — full loot is the BZ norm. Lesson: DON'T bring gear you can't afford to lose. Use T4-T5 gear in BZ until you're confident, and always remember the pro rule: 'if you're not ready to die, don't enter Black Zone'. See 🛡️ Gank Avoidance section for escape tips.

LP is a catalyst to master nodes in Destiny Board (gear, gathering, crafting) without farming full fame. 1 LP usually skips hundreds of thousands of fame. Pro tip: SPECIALIZE — focus LP on only 1-2 nodes (e.g. Skinner spec + Hide refining), DON'T spread thin across paths. LP regenerates 1 per 24h (Free) or 1 per 12h (Premium).

items.q: Asia vs Global server — can I switch?
items.a: Albion has 2 main servers: Albion East (Asia/SEA) and Albion West (NA/EU). Characters are server-locked — you can't transfer between servers. Asia (East) peak time is 13:00-15:00 UTC (21:00 WIB). If you're in Indonesia, Asia server is smoothest (50-100ms ping vs West's 200-300ms).

items.q: How long from zero to T8?
items.a: Depends on playtime + specialization. Casual player (10-15 hours/week): 3-4 months to T8. Hardcore (40+ hours/week): 6-8 weeks. Premium adds +50% fame so it can be faster. Suggestion: don't rush to T8 — enjoy progression at each tier. T6-T7 is enough for most content.

items.q: I'm a solo player, can I enjoy Albion without a guild?
items.a: Yes, many active solo players in Albion. But joining a guild gives you: tax bonus, free knowledge sharing, Mists/Hellgate party, group mat-buying. Suggestion: go solo first for 50 hours, then join a casual guild active in your time zone. Avoid ZvZ guilds if you just want chill gathering.

items.q: What's the difference between Yellow Zone, Red Zone, Black Zone?
items.a: Yellow Zone: safe, only lose durability on death. Red Zone: lose gear if killed by player (PvP allowed). Black Zone: FULL LOOT even from mob/environment death, highest reward and risk. Newbies should stick to Yellow Zone until T5-T6. See 🗺️ Zone Types Manual for full detail.

items.q: I gather but keep dying to ganks, what do I do?
items.a: 1) Bring escape kit (Stalker Hood + Royal Shoes + T4 Sticky Potion). 2) Gather in Yellow Zone first until T5. 3) Avoid peak time (13:00-15:00 UTC Asia server). 4) Scout cluster before opening full inventory. 5) Logout safe in a hidden spot if ganker is nearby. See 🛡️ Gank Avoidance Manual for full guide.

items.q: Which mount is worth buying first?
items.a: Riding Horse T3 at starting city — cheap and gives you a basic speed boost. After T4, target Swiftclaw (faster escape) or Transport Ox (hauling). T6 Direwolf optional, T8 mounts for veterans. See 🐎 Mount Guide in Beginner Essentials.

items.q: What food is mandatory for gathering?
items.a: Pork Omelette T4 — best for gathering (boosts gather yield + extra weight capacity). Use before every session. Higher tier if you can afford it. Healing Potion for emergency, Resurrection Potion MANDATORY in BZ. See 🍖 Food & Potion guide for full list.

items.q: My account got banned / hijacked, what now?
items.a: Contact official Albion support via support.albiononline.com (response 24-72h typically). Enable 2FA NOW if you haven't — most important way to protect your account. NEVER share login with anyone, including 'GM'/'admin' who DMs you (those are scammers).

items.q: Where do I pick up daily quest? Which NPC?
items.a: Talk to the Mage NPC in each Royal city (Lymhurst, Fort Sterling, Bridgewatch, Martlock, Thetford). Usually standing near city entrance or marketplace. Quest types: gather X resource, kill Y mobs, refine Z material. Reward: 30-50k silver + fame + crate. See ⏰ Daily Routine Pro for details.

items.q: What's the most profitable resource to gather right now?
items.a: Depends on real-time market conditions — check Albion Data Project. General rule: T6-T7 ore is always high-demand (for T7 gear), refined T6 Plank (Lymhurst specialty) often profitable. Avoid hoarding T8 resource if you can't afford to wait for market shifts. See 🧰 Tools & Apps for Albion Data Project link.

items.q: Fastest way to get silver as a newbie?
items.a: Newbie progression: 1) Quest line + Adventurer's Challenge (free 100-200k silver). 2) Gather T4-T5 in Yellow Zone (safe, slow but consistent). 3) Sell at marketplace daily. 4) Refine resource at specialty city for +25% bonus. 5) Don't buy T6+ gear early — focus on repairing T4-T5 gear first.

Honest answer: NO. Premium gives +50% (fame/silver) bonuses but doesn't change your PvP ability. Skill, knowledge, and dedication matter way more. Many F2P players rank top in GvG/Hellgate. Albion is a 'skill + time investment' game, not 'pay to win'.

marketplace.title: Marketplace 101
marketplace.description: Marketplace is where 80% of player money is made. Master the difference between buy/sell orders, taxes, and city arbitrage — this is the universal pro skill.

orders.how: You list an item at your price. It waits in the queue until someone buys it. Higher tax but you pick the price.
orders.when: When you have time and want max profit. Best for stacks of refined resources, gear, and rare items.

orders.how: You buy from someone else's sell order at their listed price. Pay full price immediately, no waiting.
orders.when: When you need an item NOW (gear before a fight, food before gather session). Cost is higher but instant.

orders.how: Someone posted a Buy Order at a lower price. You sell to them instantly — they get the item, you get silver fast.
orders.when: When you need silver NOW and don't want to wait. Lower profit but immediate. Good for clearing inventory.

orders.how: You post the price you're willing to pay. Sellers fulfill at your price. Patience pays — you set the rate.
orders.when: When you want bulk resources cheap (e.g. T6 wood for crafting). Wait days but save 20-30% vs Sell Orders.

taxRows.note: Paid when you place a Sell Order or Buy Order, regardless of sale outcome.
Premium cuts this in HALF. Biggest reason traders justify Premium.
Calculate this into your profit margin BEFORE listing.

city: 💎 Caerleon = highest demand for almost everything, but highest risk to travel (Black Zone access).
🌲 Lymhurst (Wood) usually sells refined Plank cheaper here — buy here, sell in Caerleon for +20-30%.
⛰️ Fort Sterling (Ore) usually has cheap Stone Block and Metal Bar.
🌊 Bridgewatch (Stone) cheap Stone resources, expensive Hide.
🍃 Martlock (Hide) cheap Hide and Leather, expensive Fiber.
🌿 Thetford (Fiber) cheap Fiber and Cloth, expensive Ore.
📊 Use Albion Data Project to check live prices across cities BEFORE traveling.
🚨 Black Market (Caerleon) buys all T4-T8 gear/consumables — sometimes 2-3x marketplace price. Mob loot tax. Best dump for crafted gear.
tips: Don't list at round numbers (10000). List at 9999 — you become first in queue.
Refresh prices every 6h — markets shift daily based on patch news and ZvZ activity.
Premium pays itself if you trade > 1M silver/week. Below that, free is fine.
Never panic sell. If prices crash, wait 2-3 days — they normalize.
Big spread Caerleon vs Royal? Travel risk is real. Use Transport Ox + scout cluster first.

routine.title: Pro Daily Routine
routine.description: Every pro Albion player has a daily ritual. Follow this checklist each login — even just 30 minutes — to compound silver, fame, and progress without burnout.

checklist.detail: Free silver + tomes daily. Click it FIRST before anything else.
Open Challenge UI, claim available rewards, plan today's progress. Weekly chest at 100% — never skip.
Talk to Mage NPC in city. 1 daily quest = free 30-50k silver + fame + loot crate.
Check gear durability. Refill food, potions, and ammo at marketplace before heading out.
Eat Pork Omelette (or higher) and drink Healing/Resurrection potions. Premium players get +50% fame buff during this window.
Gather/PvE/PvP your main money-maker. Stay in this ONE activity — context switching costs efficiency.
Deposit silver, refined resources, and rare items. NEVER log off with valuables in inventory if next session might be days away.
Sunday: complete weekly Adventurer's Challenge chest (huge silver + tomes). Check guild contribution. Sell hoarded mats.
If you're in a faction (Royal cities), grab 1 faction quest. 5 minutes, free reputation token + silver.
If you have time, jump in Mists for 30 min. Solo content = chill PvP gathering. Reset every 24h.

weekly: Complete Adventurer's Challenge weekly chest (huge tome+silver reward).
Refine at least 1 batch of resources for specialty bonus (cycle cities).
Sell hoarded gear/resources to flat marketplace (avoid hoarding > 2 weeks).
Check Murder Ledger for any new ganker in your zone.
Patch day check: read patch notes for build meta changes.
burnout: Don't try to do EVERYTHING in one session. Pick 1-2 activities and execute well.
Take 1 day off per week — your character doesn't lose anything from rest.
If you find yourself frustrated for > 30 min, log off. Bad mood = bad decisions = lost gear.
Use Sticky Notes app or phone reminder for daily quest pickup — easy to forget.
Set a weekly silver/fame goal, not a 'play every day' goal. Quality > quantity.

premium.title: Premium Math
premium.description: Should you buy Premium? Most newbies overpay or skip when they shouldn't. Here's the actual math, broken down — decide based on YOUR commitment level, not hype.

benefits.impact: T6 → T7 = ~40h vs 60h. Massive on long grinds.
Most under-rated. Solo gathering = +50% silver per session.
Halved! 1M silver sale: save 40k silver/sale. Big for traders.
Bigger island = more farm slots, more mounts, more crafting stations.
Refine 100 batches in 1h instead of 1h30. Time saved compounds.
Focus = free crafted items. More Focus = more profit.
3x more orders = 3x more passive income for traders.

cost: 🪙 Buy Premium with Gold (in-game currency): ~10 days = 1,500 gold ≈ 200-300k silver depending on rate.
💵 Buy Premium with real money: $9.99 USD/month (or cheaper via 3/6/12 month bundles).
⏰ Premium ALWAYS active 24h/7d — fame & silver bonus stack even AFK on Island.
💡 Rule of Thumb: If you play > 20 hours/week → Premium pays itself in fame + silver bonus.
scenariosYes: ✅ You play > 20h/week — fame bonus alone covers cost.
✅ You trade > 1M silver/week — halved tax pays itself.
✅ You're grinding to T7-T8 — saves dozens of hours.
✅ You actively use Focus crafting — +50% focus regen is huge.
✅ You want T2-T6 Island plots for farm/laborer income.
scenariosNo: ❌ You play < 10h/week — bonus doesn't compound enough.
❌ You only PvP or solo Mists casually — no economy interaction.
❌ You haven't decided if you'll stick with the game — wait 50h gameplay first.
tips: Start with 10 days (1500 gold) FIRST — test if bonus actually impacts you.
Bulk-buy 6 or 12 months for 10-20% discount IF you've already played 100+ hours.
Don't fall for 'Premium = required' propaganda. Free F2P is viable for casual players.
Convert silver → gold → Premium = pure F2P route. Calculate gold price vs silver value first.
Premium = QoL boost, not pay-to-win. You can compete without it if you play smart.

guides.title: Player Progression Guide
guides.description: Step-by-step path from your first hour to end-game farming. Choose the phase that matches your current progress.

beginner.title: Beginner (Pemula)
beginner.goal: Learn the controls, level up your Destiny Board, and gather T2–T4 resources in safe Royal Continent zones around your starter city.
activities: Finish the tutorial and starter quests at your starter city
Gather and craft in Blue Zones (no PvP loss)
Use the in-game map: axe icon = wood, pickaxe = ore, sickle = fiber, knife = hide, hammer = stone
Travel to your chosen Royal hub (Lymhurst, Fort Sterling, Bridgewatch, Martlock, or Thetford)
Spend Learning Points (LP) on ONE gathering branch to fast-track to T6
equipment: Gathering Tools — match your tier: T3 Adept's at level ~30, T4 Adept's enchanted .1 at ~50
Adept's Bag (T4) and Adept's Cape (T4) — extra inventory slots
Adept's Riding Horse (T3 mount) — cheap, faster than walking
Pork Omelette food — +load capacity for heavy resources
Minor Healing Potion + Resurrection Potion in slots
tips: Don't buy Premium until you understand the gameplay loop — try the free trial first
Stay in Blue/Yellow zones — Blue = no loss, Yellow = only durability damage
Focus LP on ONE gathering line first (e.g. Lumberjack only) — specialization > spreading thin
Buy a Backpack of Insight from the Adventurer's Challenge for daily silver
Asia server prime time is 13:00–15:00 UTC — gather during off-peak (21:00–09:00 UTC) for less competition

midgame.title: Mid Game
midgame.goal: Push one gathering line to T6, start farming Red Zones, dip into shallow Black Zones, and learn the market.
activities: Farm T5 in Red Zones (lower competition than Black Zones)
Try the Mists (solo) or Avalonian Roads for quick-escape gathering
Join a small guild and group-gather in T6 Black Zones
Refine your own raw resources at the matching city for the specialty bonus
Run group Hellgates 2v2 / 5v5 for silver, fame and meta gear
equipment: T5 / T6 Gathering Tools with .1 / .2 enchant — yield bonus per node
Mercenary Jacket — cast Heroic Charge on yourself for resistance + speed
Stalker Hood (solo invisibility) OR Hunter Hood (cleanse + mana)
Assassin Shoes — Ambush sprint reset for chase escape
Swiftclaw or Direwolf mount (T5/T6) — best speed-to-cost ratio
Resurrection Mage Potion + Sticky Potion — auto-revive + slow chasers
Beef Sandwich food — flat resistance buff
tips: Specialize ONE resource to T6 before opening a second branch
ALWAYS carry escape gear in your second weapon slot (Q-swap)
Sell raw resources at the matching biome city (best demand → Lymhurst for wood, Fort Sterling for ore, etc.)
Avoid solo Black Zone gathering during 13:00–15:00 UTC peak — go at night (21:00 UTC+)
Check the Killboard before entering a new Black Zone — see who's active there

endgame.title: End Game
endgame.goal: Farm T7–T8 in deep Black Zone, contribute to guild content (ZvZ / Crystal League), and master the meta.
activities: Group gathering inside Watchtower / Castle territories with guild backup
Solo or duo gather in the Mists / Avalonian Roads for quick exits
Refine T8 with Focus for huge ROI — never sell raw if you have Focus
Run Mist Bosses, Avalonian Dungeons, or Crystal League for premium loot
Use scout/spotter alt on the world map for early gank warnings
equipment: Full T7 / T8 gathering set with .3 / .4 enchant — affordable mid-end game
Stalker Hood (solo) OR Specter Hood (group invisibility for team gathering)
Mercenary Jacket OR Stalker Jacket (Q sprint reset)
Royal Boots (stamina + speed) OR Assassin Shoes (Ambush burst)
Mount: Saddled Eagle (mage-server hop), Direwolf (combat), or Spectral Bonehorse (top speed)
Major Healing Potion + Resurrection Mage Potion + Frost Bomb (instant CC escape)
Pork Omelette (load) + Wisdom of the Sphinx (focus boost for refining)
tips: Avoid solo T8 gathering during 13:00–15:00 UTC — ganker density is extreme on Asia server
Watchtower / Castle T8 spots are guild-only — get a group or expect to die
Refine T8 with Focus → 5–20× the silver of selling raw
Always have a return plan: mount + escape gear + city portal location
Carry 1× Invisibility Potion as backup — chained with Stalker Hood = double escape

professions.title: Gathering Professions
professions.description: Pick a profession on the Destiny Board. Each has its biome, tools, Royal spots (T2–T6), and Outlands hunting grounds (T7–T8).

overview.title: Gatherer Overview
overview.description: Gatherers form the backbone of Albion's economy. Every weapon, armor, and consumable starts from raw materials. Pick a path on the Destiny Board, level its tools, and choose your biome wisely.
points: Specialize ONE branch to T6 before opening a second
Bonus yield per tier from the Destiny Board (Tracking, Stealthy Collector, etc.)
Higher tier tools = faster cluster clearing time + chance for enchanted nodes
Match biome to resource for maximum yield (Forest = Wood best, Mountain = Ore best)
T5+ enchanted resources sell for 5–20× the raw tier

lumberjack.name: Lumberjack (Penebang Kayu)
lumberjack.tagline: Chop wood from Forest, Highland, and Swamp biomes.

royalSpots.zone: Bridgeoak, Holdwood (limited T6 in Royal — most is BZ)

tips: Pair with Lymhurst (Forest) — refining wood there gets the city bonus
Use Stalker Hood for instant escape — wood spots are heavily targeted
Logs are the HEAVIEST resource — Pork Omelette + max bag/cape tier essential
T7-T8 wood is usually in Forest BZ — go with guild backup
Sell planks (refined) at Lymhurst Black Market for highest profit

oreMiner.name: Ore Miner (Penambang)
oreMiner.tagline: Mine ore from Mountain and Highland biomes.

royalSpots.zone: Fort Sterling home zones (Stoneway, Mountain Cross)

tips: Fort Sterling refines ore with city specialty bonus
T8 Meteorite Ore has the highest raw silver value of any resource
Mountain biome is open / exposed — keep Stalker Hood ready for cover
Pair with Knight set (Tank build) — ore zones get heavily camped
Use Cleric Robe to cleanse focus drain debuffs from gankers

skinner.name: Skinner (Penguliti)
skinner.tagline: Skin hides from animals in Steppe, Forest, and Highland.
tips: Bridgewatch refines hide with city specialty bonus
Skinning animals adds to Killing Track too — double fame XP
T8 Direwolf Hide → end-game tank armor (Royal Plate, Specter Jacket)
Steppe is OPEN terrain — easy to spot enemies but no cover to escape
Hide is medium-weight — Master's Bag is enough

stoneQuarrier.name: Stone Quarrier (Pemecah Batu)
stoneQuarrier.tagline: Quarry stone from Highland and Mountain biomes.
tips: Martlock refines stone with city specialty bonus
Stone has the LOWEST PvP competition — best profession for solo Asia farmers
T8 Adamantium Stone is required for top-tier crafting buildings
Stone is the second-heaviest resource — Pork Omelette + extra bag tier wajib
Highland zones have Shrines (yield/speed buffs) while gathering

fiberHarvester.name: Fiber Harvester (Pemanen Serat)
fiberHarvester.tagline: Harvest fiber from Swamp and Steppe biomes.
tips: Thetford refines cloth with city specialty bonus
T8 Ghoul Yarrow → Robe of Purity and end-game cloth armor
Fiber is the LIGHTEST resource — carry max bags / silver bag
Use Cleric Robe (Purge) to cleanse root mobs in swamps
Watch for ambush mobs (snakes, vines) — they slow you for gankers

fisherman.name: Fisherman (Pemancing)
fisherman.tagline: Fish in lakes, ponds, and rivers across every biome.
fisherman.hub: Caerleon (best Black Market for rare fish) or any city with water

royalSpots.zone: Royal Continent rivers near any starter city

outlandsSpots.zone: Deep BZ lakes — rare fish + treasure chests

tips: Fishing rod is 1-handed — pair with Bag (off-hand) for max load
Use Bait (crafted from caught fish) for higher-tier catches
Spots refresh — move around, don't camp one tile
Lowest ganker risk of all professions — great for solo
Caerleon Black Market buys rare fish (Specter Carp, etc.) for big silver

tiers.title: Tier Progression Guide
tiers.description: Best strategies for each tier — from safe Royal beginner zones to dangerous T8 Outlands.

tips: Focus on leveling up your gathering tools fast — Journeyman → Adept
Use Learning Points (LP) to speed up Destiny Board progression
Don't spend too much time here — push to T3-T4 within first few hours
Red zones give higher yields but you can lose gear — bring backup
Always use Pork Omelette for max carry capacity
Gathering set (Hellion / Hunter) gives yield bonus — wear them to gather
Use Invisibility Shrines for safe travel into deeper zones
Farm off-peak (21:00–09:00 UTC) on Asia server to avoid gankers
Always plan an escape route BEFORE entering — note nearest portal
Gold Mists is great for solo T7 with quick safe exit
Avalonian Roads → group gathering with random map connections
High competition — pre-21:00 UTC is when guild groups roam
Watchtower / Castle territories are the best T8 sources — guild needed
Farm with guild backup or in hidden spots (off-meta map corners)
Expect extreme competition and constant gank attempts
T8 .3/.4 gear + Specter/Stalker Hood + escape kit is mandatory

events.dangerWindowNote: Stick to Royal Continent or farm with group

efficiency.title: Efficiency Tips
tips: Pork Omelette for carry capacity (better than Pork Pie at T6+)
Match biome to resource (Forest = Wood, Mountain = Ore, etc.)
Push ONE resource to T8 before splitting LP
Use Learning Points on the same line for fastest progression
efficiency.radiantTip: 💡 Tip: The Loot All button in Radiant Wilds speeds up PvE drop pickup!

safety.title: Safety Strategies
tips: Use Invisibility Shrines to scout deeper zones safely
Farm 21:00–09:00 UTC on Asia server for lowest ganker activity
Keep escape gear (Stalker Hood + Assassin Shoes) in slot 2 — Q-swap
Travel with guild members when possible — duo gathering is 4× safer

profitability.title: Resource Profitability
tips: Stone: Lowest competition, stable profit (great solo)
Fishing: Patient profit + rare loot bonus (Hooked Box)
Ore: Medium competition, Meteorite T8 = top silver
Hide & Fiber: High competition, swings with armor meta
